question: How do I get help for food like SNAP or other places?
answer:
## You Need Help Getting Food?  

First, **you’re not alone**—California has many ways to help families and individuals get the food they need. Below is a simple guide that walks you through the main programs, who can apply, what to bring, and what to expect.

| Program | What It Is | Who Can Use It | How You Get It |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CalFresh** (California’s SNAP) | Monthly benefit on an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card that you can use at grocery stores, some farmers markets, and online retailers. | Anyone who lives in California, is a U.S. citizen or qualified immigrant, and meets income/asset limits (limits vary by county). | Apply **online**, by phone, or in‑person at your county social services office. |
| **Women, Infants & Children (WIC)** | Free nutritious foods, nutrition counseling, and breastfeeding support for pregnant people, new moms, and kids up to age 5. | Pregnant, postpartum, or breastfeeding individuals and children up to age 5 who meet modest income guidelines. | Call your local WIC agency (see table below) or apply online where available. |
| **Local Food Banks & Pantries** | Free groceries (canned goods, fresh produce, dairy, etc.) for anyone in need. | No income test—open to anyone who is hungry. | Find a nearby pantry on **[FoodBankFinder.org](https://www.foodbankfinder.org/)** or call **2‑1‑1** (dial 2‑1‑1 from any phone). |
| **Emergency Rental & Utility Assistance (includes food dollars in some counties)** | Grants or loans to help pay rent, utilities, and sometimes grocery cards. | Varies; many programs consider income, homelessness risk, or loss of job. | Call your county’s **211** service or look on your county’s social services website. |

---

## 1. CalFresh (SNAP) – Step‑by‑Step

### Who Can Apply?
- **Adults ≥ 18** (or younger if in a household with an adult).  
- **California resident** (you must live in the state).  
- **Citizenship/Immigration:** U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or qualified non‑citizens (e.g., refugees, asylees, certain visa holders).  
- **Income:** Usually ≤ 200 % of the federal poverty level, but limits differ by **county** (some counties are a bit higher).  
- **Assets:** Low savings (generally <$2,500 for an individual, $5,000 for a couple).  

### What You Need to Bring
| Document | Why It’s Needed |
|---|---|
| **Proof of identity** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport) | Verifies who you are. |
| **Proof of residency** (utility bill, lease, or mailbox receipt) | Shows you live in California. |
| **Income proof** (most recent pay stub, unemployment benefits letter, or self‑employment records) | Shows you meet income limits. |
| **Social Security numbers** for each household member | Needed for the application. |
| **Immigration documents** (if not a citizen) | Confirms qualified status. |
| **Bank statements** (if asked) | Checks asset limits. |

### How to Apply
1. **Online:** Go to **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org/)** (or **BenefitsCal.com**) and click “Apply Now.” The portal will guide you through the questions.  
2. **Phone:** Call the **CalFresh Benefits Helpline** at **1‑877‑847‑3663** and ask to start an application.  
3. **In‑person:** Visit your **County Social Services Agency** (look up the address on your county’s website). Many offices have “express lanes” for quick intake.  

### What Happens Next?
- **Initial interview** (by phone or in person) – lasts ~15‑30 minutes.  
- **Eligibility decision** is usually sent within **7‑14 days** (some counties process faster).  
- If approved, you’ll receive an **EBT card** in the mail (often within **5‑10 business days**) and a first benefit amount right away.  

**Note:** Timelines can differ by county, so ask the staff how long they expect it to take for your area.

---

## 2. WIC – Quick Guide

| Step | What to Do |
|---|---|
| **Find your local WIC office** | Use **[WICCalifornia.org/Find](https://wiccalifornia.org/find/)** or call **1‑800‑942‑3677**. |
| **Gather documents** | Photo ID, proof of residence, proof of income (pay stub or unemployment letter), and proof of pregnancy or child’s birth certificate. |
| **Enroll** | You can often enroll **online** or by phone; an appointment may be set for a brief health screening. |
| **Receive benefits** | You’ll get a WIC card that can be used at participating stores for approved foods (milk, eggs, fruits, vegetables, cereals, etc.). |

---

## 3. Food Banks & Emergency Food Sources

- **Call 2‑1‑1** (free, 24‑hour) for a list of food pantries near you.  
- **Visit** **[FoodBankFinder.org](https://www.foodbankfinder.org/)**, type your zip code, and see hours and locations.  
- Many pantries now offer **online ordering** for “grab‑and‑go” boxes (look for “COVID‑19 pantry” or “contactless pickup”).  

**Tip:** Bring a **photo ID** if you have one, but it’s not required. If you have a **CalFresh EBT card**, you can also use it at many pantries that accept EBT.

---

## 4. Other Programs That Might Help You

| Program | What It Helps With | How to Learn More |
|---|---|---|
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Weekly cash benefits while you’re looking for work. | Apply at **[EDD.ca.gov/Unemployment](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/)**. |
| **CalWORKs** | Cash assistance for families with children, plus job‑training services. | Contact your county social services office. |
| **LIHEAP** (Low‑Income Home Energy Assistance) | Helps pay heating/cooling bills—free cash may also be used for food in some counties. | Call your county’s LIHEAP line (often listed on the county website). |
| **211** | One‑stop referral service for rent help, utility aid, medical care, legal help, and more. | Dial **2‑1‑1** or visit **[211.org](https://www.211.org/)**. |
| **Legal Aid Organizations** | Free help if you’re facing eviction, landlord issues, or discrimination. | Search “Legal Aid + [your county]” or ask 211. |

---

## 5. Quick Checklist Before You Start

- [ ] Write down the **names, addresses, and phone numbers** of *all* household members.  
- [ ] Gather **ID, residence proof, income proof, and immigration documents** (if needed).  
- [ ] Decide if you want to apply **online, by phone, or in person**.  
- [ ] Note your **county name** (e.g., Los Angeles, San Diego) – county rules can change the income limit and processing time.  
- [ ] Keep a **list of questions** for the staff (e.g., “When will I get my EBT card?”).  

---

## 6. You’re Not Alone

It can feel overwhelming, but each step you take brings you closer to having a reliable food source. **Take it one step at a time**—start with the easiest option (calling 2‑1‑1 or applying online at GetCalFresh.org). If you run into trouble, the staff at your county social services office or a local legal‑aid group can help you figure out what to do next.

**Remember:** We can’t promise an approval, but the program is there to help people *just like you* get the food they need. If you have any more questions or need a reminder of any step, feel free to ask! 

--- 

*Sources for this guide include California Department of Social Services, local county social services agencies, and national resource directories such as 2‑1‑1 and FoodBankFinder.*

question: Can I recieve multiple types of assistance at the same time?
answer:
## Can I receive more than one type of assistance at the same time?

**Yes – you can often get several public‑help programs at once, but each program has its own rules about income, assets, and how the benefits are coordinated.**  
Below is a simple guide to the most common pairings, what you’ll usually need, and how to start the process.

---

## 1. Main California Programs you might need after a job loss  

| Program | What it helps with | Typical eligibility (very basic) |
|---------|-------------------|----------------------------------|
| **CalFresh** (SNAP) | Food every month | Low household income, any citizenship status if you meet the income test. |
| **Medi‑Cal** (Medicaid) | Medical care, doctor visits, prescriptions | Very low income (often up to 138 % of the federal poverty level). |
| **CalWORKs** (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) | Cash aid, child‑care help, job‑training | Low income, must have a dependent child (or be a pregnant teen). |
| **General Assistance (GA)** | Cash aid for adults without children | Very low income, must be a resident of the county, may have property limits. |
| **SSI** (Supplemental Security Income) | Cash for people who are aged, blind, or disabled | Very low income & resources; you apply through the Social Security Administration (SSA). |
| **Section 8 / Public Housing** | Rental subsidies | Low income; you apply through the local Public Housing Authority (PHA). |
| **LIHEAP** (Low‑Income Home Energy Assistance) | Help paying heating & electric bills | Low income, must have a utility bill. |
| **WIC** (Women, Infants & Children) | Nutrition foods for pregnant women, new moms, kids | Low income, must be pregnant, breastfeeding, or have a child ≤ 5 yr. |

---

## 2. How programs work together  

| Combination | What you’ll usually get | What to watch for |
|-------------|-----------------------|-------------------|
| **CalFresh + Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Food benefits + UI cash | UI counts as income, so you must report the amount. If UI goes over the CalFresh income limit, your food benefit may be reduced. |
| **Medi‑Cal + CalWORKs** | Health coverage + cash aid | These two are **“co‑coordinated.”** Your CalWORKs cash may be lowered because Medi‑Cal already pays for many health costs. |
| **Medi‑Cal + SSI** | Full health coverage + cash for disability | If you qualify for SSI, Medi‑Cal will usually cover you automatically. |
| **GA + SSI or SSDI** | GA is **reduced** (or stopped) if you receive SSI/SSDI, because the cash aid is considered “income.” | You must tell the county right away if you start receiving SSI/SSDI. |
| **Section 8 + CalFresh** | Rent help + food help | No problem – they are separate programs. Just report all income on each application. |
| **LIHEAP + any cash program** | Energy help on top of cash aid | Usually allowed, but you still need to list all income on the LIHEAP form. |

**Key point:** *You can have many programs at once, but each one will look at the income you receive from the others.*  Always tell each agency about any new benefits you start getting.

---

## 3. Basic steps to apply for each program  

1. **Gather the same core documents for most programs**  

   | Document | Why it’s needed |
   |----------|-----------------|
   | Government‑issued ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport) | Proves who you are |
   | Social Security number (or ITIN) | Needed for income and eligibility checks |
   | Proof of residence (utility bill, lease, or letter from a landlord) | Shows you live in the county |
   | Recent pay stubs, unemployment award letter, or any other income proof | Determines how much aid you qualify for |
   | Bank statements (last 30 days) | Shows assets – many programs have limits on cash, savings, or property |
   | Proof of citizenship or legal residency (green card, visa, etc.) | Some programs only accept certain status |

2. **Apply online or in person**  

   * **CalFresh** – Apply at your county’s **CalFresh online portal** (search “County CalFresh Application”).  
   * **Medi‑Cal** – Use the **Medi‑Cal Express** website or call 1‑800‑541‑5555.  
   * **CalWORKs** – Apply at the **County Department of Social Services (DSS)** office or online portal.  
   * **General Assistance** – Visit your **County General Assistance office** (often part of DSS).  
   * **SSI** – Apply through the **Social Security Administration** website or by phone 1‑800‑772‑1213.  
   * **Section 8** – Contact your local **Public Housing Authority**; many counties have a waiting list.  
   * **LIHEAP** – Apply through the **County Social Services** office; some counties have an online form.  

3. **Interview / verification**  

   * Most programs will schedule a **phone or in‑person interview** to check your paperwork.  
   * Bring original documents (or certified copies) to the interview.  

4. **Decision & benefit start date**  

   * **Typical timelines** (can vary by county):  

     | Program | Typical decision time |
     |---------|-----------------------|
     | CalFresh | 30 days (sometimes faster if you’re on a “rapid” intake) |
     | Medi‑Cal | 2–4 weeks |
     | CalWORKs | 30–45 days |
     | GA | 45 days (some counties faster) |
     | SSI | 3–5 months (longer because it’s a federal process) |
     | Section 8 | 6 months +  (waiting list) |
     | LIHEAP | 2–4 weeks (seasonal) |

   * You’ll get a notice telling you what you’re approved for, how much, and when the first payment will start.  

5. **Keep everything up‑to‑date**  

   * If your income changes (new job, more UI, or any other cash), **report it within 10 days** to each program.  
   * If you move to a new address, tell every agency right away.  

---

## 4. Other programs that can help while you look for work  

| Program | What it does | Who might need it |
|---------|--------------|-------------------|
| **Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)** | Extra tax refund for low‑income workers | Anyone who works and files a tax return |
| **California Paid Family Leave (PFL)** | Up to 8 weeks of wage replacement for caring for a sick family member | Workers who have earned wages in the past 5 years |
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Weekly cash while you’re looking for a job | Most people who lost a job through no fault of their own |
| **Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) training** | Free job‑training programs through local **America’s Job Center** | Adults who need new skills |
| **Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)** | Help paying rent if you’re at risk of eviction | People with very low income or who lost housing due to COVID‑19 |
| **Low‑Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)** | Help with heating, cooling, or electricity bills | Those with low income and high energy costs |
| **Women, Infants & Children (WIC)** | Nutrition vouchers for pregnant women, new moms, and kids ≤ 5 yr | Low‑income mothers and babies |
| **National School Lunch Program (NSLP) & Free/Reduced‑Price Meals** | Free or cheap school meals for children | Families with school‑age kids |

These programs don’t replace cash assistance, but they can free up money for other needs.

---

## 5. Remember: **County Rules Can Differ**

* The **exact income limits, property limits, and timing** are set by each County’s Department of Social Services.  
* Some counties have **“presumptive eligibility”** – you can get temporary help while your paperwork is being checked.  
* Others may have **different waiting‑list policies** for programs like Section 8 or GA.  

**What to do:**  
1. **Visit your County’s website** (search “[Your County] CalFresh”, “[Your County] Medi‑Cal”, etc.).  
2. Call the County DSS helpline – they can tell you the specific documents and any local shortcuts.  
3. If you move to a new county, you’ll need to re‑apply for most programs there.

---

## 6. Quick Checklist for Getting Multiple Benefits

```
[ ] Write down every source of income you have (UI, part‑time work, child support, etc.)
[ ] Gather ID, SSN/ITIN, proof of residence, recent pay stubs, bank statements.
[ ] Apply for the programs you need (CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, CalWORKs, GA, etc.).
[ ] Schedule and attend any required interviews – bring original documents.
[ ] After approval, write down the start date and amount for each benefit.
[ ] Every 30 days (or sooner if you get new income), call each agency to update them.
[ ] Keep a folder with all letters, notices, and a simple spreadsheet of benefits.
```

---

## 7. Where to Get Help

* **County Department of Social Services (DSS)** – free assistance with applications.  
* **Legal Aid Foundations** – can help if you have a complex case or need an appeal.  
* **211** – dial **211** or go to **211.org** for a list of local service providers.  
* **California Department of Social Services (CDSS)** – state‑wide info and links.

---

### Bottom line
You **can receive several assistance programs at the same time**, but each program will look at the income you get from the others. By gathering the right documents, applying early, and keeping each agency informed of any changes, you can stack benefits safely and get the support you need while you search for new work.  

*If you have any specific program you want to start with, let me know and I can walk you through that application step‑by‑step.*

question: How can I get help with rent?
answer:
## Getting Help With Your Rent Losing a job can make paying rent feel impossible, but California has several programs that can give you cash or other support. Below is a simple guide that explains **what the programs are, who can apply, what you need to do, and what you’ll need to send in**. --- ### 1. Main Rental‑Assistance Programs | Program | Who Can Apply (basic) | What It Can Do | How Long It Usually Takes | |---------|----------------------|----------------|--------------------------| | **Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA) / Emergency Assistance for Rent (EAR)** – run by state and local agencies | • California residents who lost income (job loss, reduced hours, illness, etc.) 
• Rent or utility arrears that are ≤ 12 months old | One‑time cash to cover past‑due rent, security deposits, or utility bills. | 2 – 4 weeks after a complete application (may be longer in busy counties). | | **CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids)** – cash aid for families with children | • Low‑income families with a child under 18 (or 19 if in high‑school) 
• Must meet state income limits (varies by household size) | Monthly cash that can be used for rent, utilities, groceries, etc. | 3 – 6 weeks for the first benefit award; ongoing checks each month. | | **General Assistance (GA) / County Relief** – cash for adults without children | • Adults with very low income who are not eligible for CalWORKs | Cash for basic needs, including rent. | 4 – 8 weeks (depends on county). | | **Unemployment Insurance (UI) – benefits from the EDD** | • People who lost work through no fault of their own and earned enough wages in the base period. | Weekly payments that can be used toward rent. | Usually 2 weeks to start receiving checks after filing. | | **Local “Rent Relief” Grants** (often called “COVID‑ERA” or “COVID‑ECR” programs) | • Varies by city or county – many still accept new applications for the 2024‑2025 funding year. | One‑time cash, sometimes up to the full amount of past‑due rent. | 3 – 5 weeks after a complete application. | > **Note:** **Eligibility rules and funding levels change from county to county.** Always check the website or call the local agency listed in the “Where to Apply” section to get the most current information for your area. --- ### 2. Where to Apply | What to Call/Visit | How to Start | |--------------------|--------------| | **211 – California’s free information line** | Dial **211** or go to **[211.org](https://www.211.org)**. Tell them you need “rent assistance” and they will connect you with the programs in your city or county. | | **County Human Services Agency** (or “Department of Social Services”) | Search “[Your County] rent assistance” online, or go to the county website. Most counties have an “Emergency Rental Assistance” portal. | | **California Department of Social Services (CDSS) – ERA portal** | Apply online at **[https://www.edd.ca.gov/ira/](https://www.edd.ca.gov/ira/)** for state‑wide ERA funds. | | **Local HUD‑certified housing counseling agency** | Call **800‑569‑4287** or find a nearby counselor at **[HUD.gov – Housing Counseling](https://www.hud.gov/offices/hsg/sfh/hcc/hcs.cfm)**. They can help you fill out forms and avoid scams. | | **Your local public library or community center** | Many have computers and staff who can help you submit online applications. | --- ### 3. What You’ll Need to Submit | Document | Why It’s Needed | |----------|-----------------| | **Photo ID** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport) | Proves who you are. | | **Lease or rental agreement** | Shows the amount of rent you owe. | | **Proof of rent arrears** (past‑due notices, landlord letters, or a rent ledger) | Confirms how much you need help with. | | **Proof of income** (recent pay stubs, unemployment award letter, or a “no income” letter) | Determines eligibility. | | **Bank statements** (last 1‑2 months) | Shows where the assistance can be sent. | | **Utility bills** (if you’re also asking for utility help) | Shows the amount you owe. | | **Household composition** (list of people living with you, their ages, and relationship) | Needed for CalWORKs, GA, or other cash‑aid programs. | **Tip:** Keep copies (or clear photos) of every document before you send them. Most applications let you upload PDFs or photos directly. --- ### 4. Step‑by‑Step Checklist 1. **Talk to your landlord or lender right away** – many will let you set up a payment plan while you wait for aid. 2. **Call 211** (or text “311” if your county offers a text service). Ask for “Emergency Rental Assistance”. 3. **Write down the phone number or web link** for the local agency the 211 worker gives you. 4. **Gather the documents** listed above. 5. **Complete the online or paper application** (most counties now use an online portal). 6. **Submit copies of all documents** with your application. 7. **Follow up** – call the agency after about **7‑10 days** to confirm they received everything and to ask about the timeline. 8. **If approved**, the agency will either send you a check or pay the landlord/utility company directly. 9. **Keep a record** of every payment you receive and any communication with your landlord. --- ### 5. Timelines & What to Expect | Stage | Typical Time Frame | |-------|--------------------| | **Initial contact (211 or county office)** | Same day – you’ll get a case number. | | **Application review** | 2‑4 weeks (depends on volume and county). | | **Decision & payment** | Usually within 1‑2 weeks after approval. | | **If you need more help** | Re‑apply or ask the caseworker about “additional rent assistance” or “utility assistance” programs. | If you do **not** get approved for a particular program, the agency will often tell you about **other options** (like GA, CalFresh, or LIHEAP) that might still help. --- ### 6. Other Programs You Might Need | Need | Program | How to Apply | |------|---------|--------------| | **Utility bills** (electric, gas, water) | **LIHEAP – Low‑Income Home Energy Assistance Program** | Call 211 or go to **[www.caldhhs.org/liheap](https://www.caldhhs.org/liheap)**. | | **Food** | **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Apply online at **[https://www.getcalfresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org)** or call 211. | | **Health coverage** | **Medi‑Cal** | Apply at **[Covered CA](https://www.coveredca.com)** or via your county social services office. | | **Job search & training** | **America’s Job Center** (local Workforce Development Board) | Find your nearest center at **[www.careeronestop.org](https://www.careeronestop.org)**. | | **If you’re at risk of homelessness** | **HUD homeless assistance list** & **local shelters** | Call **1‑800‑RING‑HOME (1‑800‑746‑4663)** or check **[HUD.gov/homeless](https://www.hud.gov/homeless)**. | | **Legal help with landlords** | **HUD‑certified housing counseling** or **legal aid nonprofits** | Call **211** or search “legal aid housing California”. | --- ## Quick Summary (5‑Step Cheat Sheet) 1. **Call 211** now – ask for “rent assistance”. 2. **Get the local agency’s name** and write down the web link or phone number. 3. **Collect your ID, lease, rent‑due notice, and proof of income**. 4. **Fill out the online application** (or paper form) and upload the documents. 5. **Follow up in 1‑2 weeks**; if approved, the money goes to you or directly to your landlord. You’re not alone—many Californians are in the same spot, and the state has money set aside to help. Keep your documents ready, stay in touch with the agency, and don’t hesitate to call 211 again if you need another type of aid. Good luck, and take it one step at a time!

question: Are there programs that I could qualify for to help me get another job?
answer:
## You Can Get Help Finding Your Next Job Losing a job is stressful, but California has many programs that can give you money **and** training while you look for new work. Below is a simple guide (5th‑grade reading level) to the main options, who can apply, what you need, and how to start. --- ### 1. Unemployment Insurance (UI) – **“Unemployment Benefits”** | What it is | Money you can receive while you look for work. | |------------|-----------------------------------------------| | **Who can apply?** | Anyone who lost a job **through no fault of their own** (lay‑off, hours cut, etc.). Even if you think you might have been fired or quit, you can still apply – the state will decide. | | **Key eligibility basics** | • You were **physically able** to work and **available** for work.
• You are **looking for work every week** and can show proof (e.g., job‑search log).
• You earned enough wages in the **last 18 months** (the “base period”). | | **How to apply** | 1️⃣ Gather your personal info (SSN, driver’s license, address, phone).
2️⃣ **Apply online** at the California Employment Development Department (EDD) – [EDD Unemployment portal](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/).
3️⃣ **Register** in **CalJOBS** (the state job‑search system).
4️⃣ Submit required documents (see below).
5️⃣ **Certify** each two‑week claim period (online or by phone). | | **Documents you’ll need** | • Most recent pay stubs or W‑2s (show earnings).
• Your employer’s name, address, and dates you worked.
• Proof of identity (driver’s license, state ID, or passport). | | **Timeline** | Processing usually takes **about 3 weeks** for the first payment. After that, you’ll get money **every two weeks** as long as you keep certifying. | | **Extra tip** | While you receive UI, you can also enroll in **California Training Benefits (CTB)** to get tuition help for approved training programs. See the next section. | --- ### 2. California Training Benefits (CTB) – **“Training While You Get UI”** | What it is | Funding that pays for *approved* job‑training courses *while* you are on UI. | |------------|---------------------------------------------| | **Who can use it?** | UI claimants who are **approved** for CTB by the EDD. You must be willing to **stop looking for a job** for the training period, then return to job‑search after the program ends. | | **Basic steps** | 1️⃣ **Ask the EDD** (when you certify) if you’re eligible for CTB.
2️⃣ Choose a **CTB‑approved training program** (see list on the EDD website or at your local **Workforce Development Board**).
3️⃣ Submit the **CTB application** with a training plan.
4️⃣ Once approved, the EDD will pay the tuition *directly* to the school. | | **Docs you’ll need** | • Proof of UI claim (your UI claim number).
• Official acceptance letter from the training provider.
• Any prerequisite certificates (e.g., high‑school diploma or GED). | | **Timeline** | Approval can take **2‑4 weeks** after you submit the application. Payments are made directly to the school once approved. | | **County note** | Each county’s **Local Workforce Development Board (LWDB)** may have its own list of approved schools and may offer additional “local training grants.” Call your county LWDB to confirm which programs are available in *your* area. | --- ### 3. CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids) | What it is | Cash assistance for families with children, plus **job‑training, childcare, and transportation** help. | |------------|-----------------------------------------------------------| | **Who can apply?** | Low‑income families with **minor children** (under 18). You may also qualify if you are pregnant. | | **Eligibility basics** | • Income and assets below a **county‑specific limit** (limits vary, so check with your county office).
• You must be a **California resident** and willing to work or attend training. | | **How to start** | 1️⃣ Call your **County Human Services Agency (HSA)** or visit the local office.
2️⃣ Fill out the **CalWORKs application** (online or paper).
3️⃣ Provide income proof, ID, and proof of children’s residency (birth certificates, school records). | | **Key benefits** | • Monthly cash assistance.
• **Childcare vouchers** while you attend school or training.
• **Transportation assistance** (bus passes, mileage).
• **Job‑training vouchers** (often linked to local community colleges). | | **Docs you’ll need** | • Proof of income (pay stubs, unemployment benefits award letter, SSI/SSDI award).
• Proof of residency (utility bill, lease).
• Child birth certificates or school records. | | **Timeline** | After you submit a complete application, you’ll usually get a decision **within 30 days**. Benefits, if approved, start within a few weeks of the decision. | | **County note** | The amount of cash help and the specific training programs **vary by county**. Ask the HSA in your county for the exact list. | --- ### 4. SNAP (Food Stamps) – **“Help Buying Groceries”** | What it is | Monthly benefit card to buy food. | |------------|-----------------------------------| | **Who can apply?** | Any California resident with **low income**, including UI recipients, CalWORKs families, and seniors. | | **Basic eligibility** | • Income < **165 % of the Federal Poverty Level** (exact amount changes each year).
• Resources (bank accounts, etc.) usually must be < $2,250 (higher if you have a home). | | **How to apply** | 1️⃣ Go to **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org/)** and start the online application.
2️⃣ Or call **County SNAP office** (look up your county’s number). | | **Docs you’ll need** | • ID (driver’s license, state ID).
• Proof of income (UI award letter, pay stubs, or unemployment benefits).
• Proof of rent/mortgage and utilities (to verify expenses). | | **Timeline** | Most people receive a decision **within 30 days**; approved households often get the EBT card **within a week** after approval. | | **County note** | Some counties run **“SNAP Outreach”** programs that can help you apply in person or online with a caseworker. | --- ### 5. Medicaid (Medi‑Cal) – **“Free or Low‑Cost Health Care”** | What it is | Health coverage for low‑income Californians. | |------------|----------------------------------------------| | **Who can apply?** | Anyone with income below **138 % of the Federal Poverty Level** (or higher if you qualify under other rules). UI recipients, CalWORKs families, pregnant people, seniors, and people with disabilities often qualify. | | **How to apply** | • Online at **[Covered California](https://www.coveredca.com/)** (choose “Medi‑Cal”).
• Call **1‑877‑502‑7372** or visit your **County Social Services office**. | | **Docs you’ll need** | • Proof of identity (ID).
• Proof of income (UI award letter, pay stubs).
• Proof of residency (lease, utility bill). | | **Timeline** | Usually **within 30 days** of a complete application; coverage can begin the first day of the month after approval. | | **County note** | Some counties have **Medi‑Cal enrollment clinics** that can help you finish paperwork on the spot. | --- ### 6. Local Workforce Development Boards (LWDB) – **“County Job‑Training & Career Services”** | What they do | Offer free career counseling, resume help, job‑search workshops, and **locally‑funded training vouchers**. | |--------------|------------------------------------------------------------| | **How to find yours** | Search “**[your county] Workforce Development Board**” or call **211** (the state information line) for the phone number. | | **Typical services** | • One‑on‑one career coach.
• Free **resume‑building** and interview practice.
• Information on **apprenticeships**, **community‑college certificate programs**, and **short‑term trades** (e.g., HVAC, welding, IT).
• **Child‑care** and **transportation vouchers** for training participants. | | **Eligibility** | Usually open to anyone **unemployed or under‑employed** in the county; some programs have income limits, but many are **free for all residents**. | | **Docs you may need** | • Photo ID.
• Proof of residence (utility bill, lease).
• Proof of income (if the specific program has a limit). | | **Timeline** | You can usually walk‑in or schedule a **same‑day appointment**; training vouchers may take a few weeks to process. | | **County note** | **Programs differ by county** (e.g., San Diego may focus on biotech, while Fresno emphasizes agriculture). Ask your LWDB for a printed list of current courses. | --- ## Quick “What‑to‑Do” Checklist | Step | Action | Where to do it | |------|--------|----------------| | **1** | **Apply for UI** (unemployment benefits). | Online at the **EDD** site. | | **2** | **Register in CalJOBS** (required for UI). | After UI claim, on the **EDD** portal. | | **3** | **Ask about CTB** (training while on UI). | When you certify UI every two weeks. | | **4** | **Contact your county LWDB** for free job‑training and career counseling. | Search “*Your County* Workforce Development Board” or dial **211**. | | **5** | **Apply for SNAP** (food assistance). | Online at **GetCalFresh.org**. | | **6** | **Apply for Medi‑Cal** (health coverage). | Online via **Covered California** or your county social services office. | | **7** | **If you have children**, consider **CalWORKs** for cash help, childcare, and training vouchers. | Call your County Human Services Agency. | | **8** | **Gather documents** (ID, income proof, residence proof) and keep them in one folder. | Physical folder or digital folder on your phone/computer. | | **9** | **Certify UI** every two weeks and keep a **job‑search log** (list of places you applied, contacts you spoke to). | Online at EDD portal. | | **10**| **Stay in touch** with the caseworkers you meet—ask them what the next steps are and when to expect a decision. | Phone or email. | --- ## Other Helpful Programs (Even If You Haven’t Asked About Them) | Program | What it Helps With | Who Might Qualify | |---------|-------------------|-------------------| | **Housing Assistance (Section 8, Emergency Rental Assistance)** | Pays part of your rent or helps you avoid eviction. | Low‑income households, UI recipients, CalWORKs families. | | **Veterans’ Benefits (VA, CalVet)** | Job training, education vouchers, health care for veterans. | Anyone who served in the armed forces. | | **Disability Benefits (SSI, SSDI, California Disability Service Center)** | Cash assistance and health coverage for people with a disabling condition. | Those with a qualifying disability. | | **College Tuition Waiver (College Promise, Community College Fees Waiver)** | Free community‑college tuition for eligible low‑income adults. | Usually requires income below a set level and may need a FAFSA. | | **Apprenticeship Programs** | Paid on‑the‑job training in trades (construction, electrical, automotive, etc.). | Open to most adults; many have no income limit. | --- ## Remember… * **Applying does not hurt you.** Even if you later find out you don’t qualify, the agency will let you know. * **Keep copies** of every form you send and every email you receive. * **Ask for help** – your county’s **LWDB**, **Human Services Agency**, or the **EDD** all have staff who can walk you through each step. * **Every county is a little different.** That’s why we always say *“check with your local office for exact rules and program lists.”* You’re not alone—California has a safety net that can give you money, health care, food, and training while you look for the next great job. Take one step at a time, and keep moving forward. Good luck! 🌟

question: What are the income limits for Unemployment Insurance?
answer:
## Unemployment Insurance – How Income Affects Your Benefit  

**You don’t need a set “income limit” to qualify.**  
Instead, the state looks at **how much you earned in a recent 12‑month “base period.”** If you earned enough wages during that time, you may be eligible for benefits. The amount you receive each week is then **calculated from those earnings** – the more you earned, the higher the weekly benefit (up to a maximum set by the state).

### What the State Checks  

| Requirement | What It Means for You |
|-------------|----------------------|
| **Base‑period earnings** | You must have earned a minimum amount of wages during the base period (the first four of the last five completed quarters). The exact figure changes each year, so the EDD’s online calculator will tell you if you meet it. |
| **Recent work history** | You need to be **totally or partially unemployed** through no fault of your own, and you must be **physically able, available, and actively looking for work** each week. |
| **Legal work status** | You must have a Social Security number and be authorized to work in the U.S. (or be a U.S. citizen). |

### How to Find Out If You Meet the Earnings Requirement  

1. **Gather your recent pay information** – recent pay stubs, W‑2s, or 1099s that show your wages for the last 12 months.  
2. **Use the EDD’s Unemployment Benefit Calculator** – it is an online tool that asks for your wage totals and tells you:  
   * Whether you meet the base‑period earnings test.  
   * An estimate of your weekly benefit amount.  

   👉 [Unemployment Benefit Calculator](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/benefit-calculator)  

3. **Apply online** – When you start an UI claim, the system will automatically pull the wage information you entered and confirm if you qualify.

### Documents You’ll Need When You Apply  

- **Social Security number**  
- **Proof of recent earnings** (pay stubs, W‑2, 1099, or a recent tax return)  
- **Proof of identity** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)  

### Timeline  

| Step | How Long It Usually Takes |
|------|---------------------------|
| **Submit the online claim** | Minutes (you can start right away) |
| **EDD reviews earnings & eligibility** | About **3 weeks** for the first payment, if everything is complete |
| **Weekly certification** | Every 2 weeks after you start receiving benefits (you tell the EDD you’re still looking for work) |

### County‑Specific Notes  

- The **core eligibility rules are the same statewide**, but some counties may offer **additional “training” or “work‑share” programs** that can affect how you certify each week.  
- If you live in a **large urban county (e.g., Los Angeles, San Diego, San Francisco)**, you might see extra resources for job‑search workshops or local hiring events.  
- Always check your county’s **American Job Center** or the local **EDD office** for any extra help that’s available where you live.

### Other Programs That Might Help While You’re Unemployed  

| Program | Who It Helps | What It Offers |
|---------|--------------|----------------|
| **California Training Benefits (CTB)** | UI claimants who want to go back to school or vocational training | Allows you to receive UI benefits while you’re in an approved training program. |
| **State Disability Insurance (SDI)** | Workers who become temporarily disabled | Provides partial wage replacement if you can’t work due to illness or injury. |
| **CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids)** | Low‑income families with children | Cash assistance, food, and childcare support while you’re looking for work. |
| **California Earned Income Tax Credit (CalEITC)** | Low‑to‑moderate‑income workers | A refundable tax credit that can boost your tax refund (available even if you’re receiving UI). |
| **Covered California health insurance subsidies** | Anyone who lost employer health coverage | May qualify for lower‑cost health plans based on your income. |

### Quick Checklist Before You Start  

- ✅ Have your **Social Security number** ready.  
- ✅ Collect **pay stubs, W‑2s, or 1099s** from the past 12 months.  
- ✅ Make a **list of the jobs you’re applying for** (you’ll need to report this each week).  
- ✅ Find a **computer or smartphone with internet access** to apply online (or call the UI hotline if you need help).  

---

### Need More Help?  

- **Visit the EDD website** for step‑by‑step guides and the benefit calculator.  
- Call the **UI Customer Service line** at **1‑800‑300‑5616** (available in English and Spanish).  
- Look for a local **American Job Center** for free job‑search assistance and training info.  

Remember, you’re not alone—many Californians go through this process, and there are resources to help you get back to work and keep your finances stable while you do. 🌟

question: Where do I apply for CalWORKs benefits?
answer:
## How to Apply for **CalWORKs** Benefits  

You can apply for CalWORKs (California’s cash‑aid program) **online or in person**.  

| **Method** | **What to Do** | **What Happens Next** |
|------------|----------------|-----------------------|
| **Online** | Go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.benefitscal.com)** and click **“Apply for CalWORKs.”** | A county worker will call you (usually within 1‑2 weeks) to set up an eligibility interview. |
| **In‑Person** | Find the **County Social Services Agency** (also called “County Welfare Office”) in the county where you live. | Bring your paperwork to the office; a staff member will start your interview right away. |

### Steps to Get Started  

1. **Gather Needed Papers** (see list below).  
2. **Create an online account** at BenefitsCal.com **or** go to your local office.  
3. **Fill out the application** – answer all questions honestly.  
4. **Schedule and attend an eligibility interview** (phone or in‑person).  
5. **Wait for a decision** – most counties let you know within a few weeks.  

### Common Documents You'll Need  

| Document | Why It’s Needed |
|----------|----------------|
| **Photo ID** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport) | Proves who you are. |
| **Proof of residence** (utility bill, lease, or letter from a landlord) | Shows you live in the county you’re applying to. |
| **Social Security numbers** for everyone in the household | Required for income checks. |
| **Recent pay stubs or proof of unemployment** (if you worked recently) | Shows your current income. |
| **Bank statements** (last 30 days) | Helps determine resources. |
| **Proof of child’s age** (birth certificate or school records) | CalWORKs is for families with kids under 18 (or pregnant). |
| **Any other public assistance letters** (e.g., CalFresh, SSI) | Shows other benefits you may already receive. |

*You don’t need to bring everything at first, but be ready to provide them if asked.*

### How Long Does It Take?  

- **Application submission:** immediate (online) or the day you visit the office.  
- **Eligibility interview:** usually within 1‑2 weeks of applying.  
- **Decision:** most counties give a written notice within **30 days** of the interview, but times can vary.

### Important Note About Counties  

California has **58 counties**, and each county runs its own CalWORKs office.  
- **Eligibility rules are the same statewide**, but the **exact paperwork requirements, interview scheduling, and wait‑times can differ**.  
- If you move to a new county, you’ll need to re‑apply there.

### Other Programs That Might Help You  

| Program | Who Can Apply | What It Provides |
|---------|---------------|------------------|
| **CalFresh** (food stamps) | Low‑income households, including those on CalWORKs | Monthly grocery assistance. |
| **Medi‑Cal** (California Medicaid) | Low‑income families, pregnant people, children | Free or low‑cost health coverage. |
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | People who lost a job through no fault of their own | Weekly cash payments while you look for work. |
| **General Assistance (GA)** | Adults without children who don’t qualify for CalWORKs | Cash aid for basic living costs. |
| **Housing Assistance (e.g., Emergency Rental Assistance)** | Families facing a rent or utility crisis | Money to help keep a home. |

You can apply for many of these programs **through the same BenefitsCal.com portal** or at your county social services office.

---

#### Need More Help?  

- Call your **County Social Services Agency** (look up the phone number on the county’s website).  
- Ask for a **“CalWORKs intake specialist”** – they can walk you through the process step‑by‑step.  

You’re not alone—many Californians have been in your shoes, and the county agencies are there to help you get the support you need. 🌟

question: Laid off this month. I need help paying for food. Can I get help quickly? What can I qualify for and how do I apply in my county?
answer:
## Quick Help for Food (CalFresh)

**You can apply for CalFresh right now.**  
CalFresh gives you an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card that you can use to buy groceries.

### What You Might Qualify For
| What you get | When you can get it |
|--------------|--------------------|
| **Monthly food benefits** (about $0‑$400 depending on your household) | Usually **within 2‑4 weeks** after you finish the eligibility interview. |
| **Expedited (fast‑track) benefits** if you have very low income or no money at all | May be approved in **as little as 1‑2 weeks**.  

> **Note:** Exact amounts and speed can differ from county to county. Your local county office will tell you the exact timeline.

---

## Who Can Get CalFresh?

| Requirement | Simple explanation |
|-------------|--------------------|
| **You live in California** | Must be a California resident. |
| **You have little or no income** | If you were laid off, the money you got in the last 30 days is counted. Any income you still receive (like part‑time work or unemployment) is also counted. |
| **You are a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or have a qualifying immigration status** | If you’re not sure, ask the county worker. |
| **You have limited resources** | Usually cash, a bank account, or a vehicle worth less than a set amount. The county will tell you the exact limit. |

You do **not** need to wait for a job to start again—being laid off now is enough to apply.

---

## How to Apply in Your County

1. **Start the application online**  
   • Go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.benefitscal.com)** (the state portal).  
   • Choose **“Apply for CalFresh”** and fill out the short questionnaire.

2. **Submit required information**  
   • Name, address, phone, and household members.  
   • Your **most recent pay stubs or a copy of your final paycheck** (last 30 days).  
   • If you don’t have a paper proof, write a short letter that says:  
     - The date you stopped working,  
     - That you are not receiving any more wages,  
     - Your signature and date.

3. **Wait for the county interview**  
   • Your county social services office will call you **within 1‑2 weeks**.  
   • The interview can be over the phone or in person.  
   • Have your ID, proof of address (utility bill or lease), and the income proof ready.

4. **Get your EBT card**  
   • If approved, the county will mail you an EBT card (sometimes in 5‑7 business days).  
   • Benefits are loaded each month.

---

## Documents You’ll Need

| Document | Why it’s needed |
|----------|-----------------|
| **Photo ID** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport) | Proves who you are. |
| **Proof of California residency** (utility bill, lease, or mail) | Shows you live in the state. |
| **Proof of income stopped** (final paycheck, lay‑off notice, or a written letter) | Shows your recent earnings. |
| **Social Security numbers** for everyone in the household | Required for eligibility check. |
| **Bank statements or proof of cash assets** (if asked) | Checks resource limits. |

If you can’t get any of these right away, tell the county worker. They often accept a signed statement explaining the missing item.

---

## Timeline (What to Expect)

| Step | Typical time |
|------|--------------|
| **Online application submitted** | Same day |
| **County calls for interview** | 1‑2 weeks |
| **Eligibility decision** | Up to **30 days** (faster if you qualify for expedited service) |
| **EBT card mailed** | 5‑7 business days after approval |
| **First benefit load** | Usually the next month after you get the card |

If you haven’t heard back after **2 weeks**, call your county office (phone numbers are on the BenefitsCal website).

---

## County‑Specific Note

*Each California county runs its own CalFresh office.*  
- Some counties have **in‑person offices**, others handle everything by phone or online.  
- The exact **phone number, address, and wait times** can differ.  

**What to do:** After you finish the online form, the system will show the contact info for **your county’s Social Services Agency**. Keep that number handy.

---

## Other Programs That May Help Right Now

| Program | What it helps with | How to apply |
|--------|-------------------|--------------|
| **CalWORKs** (if you have children or are a family) | Cash for food, housing, utilities, clothing, medical care | Apply on **BenefitsCal.com** or call your county social services office. |
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Weekly cash while you look for a new job | Apply at **[EDD California](https://edd.ca.gov)**. |
| **Local Food Banks** | Free groceries and meals | Find the nearest one with **[FoodBankFinder.org](https://www.foodbankfinder.org)** or call **2‑1‑1**. |
| **211 – Community Resource Helpline** | Referrals for emergency rent, utilities, childcare, health care, and more | Dial **2‑1‑1** (or visit **[211.org](https://www.211.org)**). |
| **Emergency Rental Assistance** (city or county programs) | Money to help you pay rent or utilities while you’re between jobs | Call your county office or 2‑1‑1 to learn about local programs. |

---

### You’re Not Alone

Losing a job is stressful, but help is available. Start the CalFresh application today, keep your documents ready, and reach out to **2‑1‑1** if you need food right away. The county workers are there to guide you step‑by‑step.  

**Good luck, and take one step at a time—you’ve got this!**

question: Where can I get help finding a job in California after a layoff, and do they connect to benefits?
answer:
## Where to Find Job‑Help After a Layoff  

| Resource | What It Does | How to Reach It |
|----------|--------------|-----------------|
| **America’s Job Center of California (AJCC)** | Free in‑person help: job listings, resume workshops, interview practice, and connections to local employers. | Find the nearest center on the **EDD “Jobs & Training”** page or call 1‑800‑480‑3289. |
| **CalJOBS (online)** | State job‑board where you can post a resume, search openings, and sign up for training programs. | Go to **[CalJOBS.org](https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs_and_training/Caljobs/)** and create an account. |
| **EDD Layoff Services** | Phone and online counselors who give you a step‑by‑step plan after a layoff, including benefit information. | Call the Unemployment Insurance (UI) line at **1‑800‑300‑5616** (TTY 1‑800‑815‑9387) for a live specialist. |
| **Local Workforce Development Board** | County‑level office that runs job‑training programs, apprenticeship links, and sometimes transportation help. | Look up your county’s “Workforce Development Board” on the **EDD website** or ask the AJCC staff. |
| **Veterans’ Employment Resources** (if you served) | Tailored job‑search tools, resume help, and connections to veteran‑friendly employers. | Visit the **EDD “Veterans”** page or call the VA’s employment line. |
| **People with Disabilities Services** | Specialized job‑coaching, assistive‑technology help, and employer outreach. | Contact the **Disability Services** section on the EDD site. |

### Do These Services Connect to Benefits?  

Yes! Most of the places above also help you **apply for or keep your unemployment benefits** while you look for work.

* When you register on **CalJOBS**, the EDD will automatically check that you have posted a resume. If you miss the deadline, they may pause your UI payments.  
* AJCC staff can walk you through the **UI application**, help fix any errors, and remind you to **certify** each week so you keep getting money.  
* Some local workforce boards run **California Training Benefits** (CTB) that let you take a class **and still receive UI** at the same time.

---

## Quick Guide: Steps After a Layoff  

1. **Gather Your Information**  
   * Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID)  
   * Social Security number  
   * Most recent pay stub or “last pay” statement  
   * Letter or email from your employer that says you were laid off (if you have it)  

2. **Apply for Unemployment Insurance (UI)**  
   * **Online:** log in to **myEDD** (fastest).  
   * **Phone or mail:** use the numbers in source 10 if you need language help.  

3. **Register on CalJOBS (within 21 days)**  
   * Create a profile, upload a resume, and start looking at job listings.  

4. **Visit Your Nearest AJCC**  
   * Bring the documents above.  
   * Ask for help with resume, interview practice, and any local training programs.  

5. **Certify Weekly for UI**  
   * Log in to **myEDD** every two weeks, answer the short questionnaire, and keep getting payments.  

6. **Explore Training or Education**  
   * If you want to go back to school, ask about **California Training Benefits** – you can stay on UI while you study.  

---

## What You’ll Need to Bring to an AJCC or Workforce Office  

| Document | Why It Helps |
|----------|--------------|
| Photo ID | Proves who you are. |
| Social Security card or number | Needed for benefit payments. |
| Recent pay stub or final pay statement | Shows your recent earnings (used to calculate UI). |
| Layoff notice or email from employer | Confirms you lost your job “through no fault of your own.” |
| Proof of residency (utility bill, lease) | Some county programs require it. |
| Resume (if you have one) | Staff can give you quick feedback. |

If you can’t get a specific paper, **write a short note** that explains what’s missing (e.g., “I don’t have a formal layoff letter, but my last work day was May 15, 2025”) and sign it. Staff are used to helping with missing items.

---

## How Long Does It Take?  

| Step | Approximate Time |
|------|------------------|
| UI application processing | **2–3 weeks** for the first payment (you’ll get an email with the exact date). |
| CalJOBS registration | **Same day** if you have internet; must be done within 21 days of the notice you receive from EDD. |
| AJCC appointment | Usually **same‑day or next‑day** walk‑in; some offices let you book online. |
| Weekly UI certification | **A few minutes** each two‑week period (online). |

---

## County‑Specific Note

Below is a simple guide to the biggest things you can do today and in the next few weeks. --- ## 1. Talk to Someone Right Now | Situation | Phone / Online help | When to use it | |-----------|--------------------|----------------| | **Feeling very sad, hopeless, or thinking about hurting yourself** | Call **988 – Suicide & Crisis Lifeline** (or dial 988, then press 1 for the Disaster Distress Helpline).
You can also text **988** to start a chat. | Any time you feel unsafe or need immediate emotional support. | | **General stress, anxiety, or just need to talk** | Call **211** (dial 211) – a free service that can connect you to a local counselor, food pantry, or housing help. | Anytime you want a listening ear or help finding local resources. | | **If you are in immediate danger (e.g., you feel you might harm yourself or are unsafe at home)** | Call **911**. | Emergency only. | --- ## 2. If you get a request for more info, respond quickly to avoid delays. --- ## 3. Emergency Rent & Utility Help Many counties in California run **Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)** programs that can pay part or all of your rent and utility bills for a few months. **How it works (county‑by‑county)** | What you’ll need | Typical steps | Note | |------------------|---------------|------| | Proof you lost income (UI claim, termination letter, or paycheck stub) | 1. Food Assistance – CalFresh If you’re struggling to buy groceries, **CalFresh** (California’s SNAP program) gives you an electronic benefit card to buy food at grocery stores. | Requirement | Details | |-------------|---------| | **Income** | Usually at or below 200 % of the federal poverty level, but many counties have higher limits for people receiving UI. | | **Residency** | You must live in California. | | **Work requirement** | If you’re able, you must be looking for work (UI counts toward this). | **How to apply** 1. Go to **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org/)**. 2. Create an account and fill out the online form (about 15‑20 minutes). 3. Upload a copy of your **UI benefit notice** or a recent pay stub, plus photo ID. **When you’ll get help** – Most people receive their first benefit **within 30 days** of a complete application. --- ## 5. Health Coverage – Medi‑Cal If you lost employer health insurance, you may qualify for **Medi‑Cal**, California’s Medicaid program. | Who can apply | What you need | |---------------|---------------| | Residents with **low income** (often up to 138 % of the federal poverty level) or those who are **receiving UI** | Proof of income (UI notice or recent pay stub), photo ID, and proof of California residency (lease or utility bill). | **How to apply** - **Online:** **[Covered California – Medi‑Cal enrollment](https://www.coveredca.com/medi-cal/)**. - **Phone:** Call **1‑800‑300‑1506** (Spanish available). **Start of coverage:** Usually **within 30‑45 days** after your application is approved. --- ## 6. Quick “What to Do First” Checklist | # | Action | Why it matters | |---|--------|----------------| | 1 | **Call 988** if you feel unsafe or very depressed. | Immediate emotional safety. | | 2 | **Apply for Unemployment Insurance** on the EDD website today. | Starts weekly cash flow. | | 3 | **Call 211** or visit your county ERA site to start a rent‑help application. | Keeps a roof over your head. | | 4 | **Apply for CalFresh** online (GetCalFresh.org). | Helps with groceries. | | 5 | **Check Medi‑Cal eligibility** and apply if needed. | Keeps you healthy. | | 6 | **Create a CalJOBS account** and upload your resume. | Begins the job search. | | 7 | **Contact a HUD housing counselor** if you have an eviction notice. | Gets you professional help with your landlord. | --- ### You’re Not Alone All of these steps can feel overwhelming, but taking them **one at a time** makes it manageable. Keep a notebook (or a phone note) with: - Dates you applied or called. - Confirmation numbers or emails you receive. - What documents you still need. If you ever get “stuck,” call **211** again – they can walk you through any step or connect you to a local caseworker. **Take care of yourself, and keep reaching out. Help is out there, and you deserve it.** 🌼

## 📦 Quick Help for Food (CalFresh) | What it is | A state program that gives you a **monthly cash card** to buy groceries. | |------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------| | **Can you get it fast?** | Yes! Many counties offer **Emergency CalFresh** – you can get a benefit card in **as little as 7‑10 days** while your full application is processed. | | **Who can apply?** | • You are a California resident
• You have children (or a dependent)
• Your household income is low – the amount you earn from work, unemployment, or severance must be **under the CalFresh limit** (the exact limit changes by county). | | **What you need to send** | See the table below. Gather these before you start the application. | | **How to apply** | 1. Go to **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org)** and click **“Apply Now.”**
2. You can also call **+1‑877‑847‑3663** or visit your **county social services office** in person.
3. Fill out the short online form, upload the documents, and submit. | | **How long it takes** | • **Emergency CalFresh:** 7‑10 days for the first card.
• **Regular CalFresh:** Usually **30 days** after the county gets all your paperwork. | | **What to do if you move** | Tell the county you’re moving **right away**. If you move to a new county, you’ll transfer your case (or re‑apply) with the new office. Wait times can differ, so apply as soon as you have a new address. | ### Documents Usually Needed | Document | Why it’s needed | Example | |----------|----------------|---------| | **Photo ID** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport) | Proves who you are | California driver’s license | | **Proof of residence** | Shows you live in California | Utility bill, lease, or a letter from your mom if you move in with her | | **Proof of income** | County checks that income is below the limit | Recent pay stubs, unemployment award letter, or a severance notice | | **Proof of children** | Determines household size | Birth certificates, school ID, or a custody document | | **Bank statement or proof of low savings** | Shows you don’t have a lot of money saved | Recent bank print‑out (if asked) | *If you can’t get a particular paper, write a short note explaining why and sign it. Counties often accept a simple letter.* --- ## 🎯 How Unemployment Insurance (UI) & Severance Pay Fit In | Situation | Effect on CalFresh | |-----------|-------------------| | **You are **receiving UI** (the weekly check from EDD)** | UI counts as **income**. As long as the amount you get each month stays **below the CalFresh limit**, you can still get CalFresh. The UI money does **not reduce** the amount of CalFresh you receive, but it is considered when the county decides how much to give you. | | **You have **not started receiving UI yet** (just filed a claim)** | You **don’t need** to report the pending claim on your CalFresh application. Once you start getting the money, tell the county right away. | | **You received **severance pay** (a lump‑sum from your former employer)** | Severance is treated like regular earnings. It is counted as **income for the month you receive it**. If the amount pushes your household’s monthly income over the CalFresh limit, your benefit for that month could be reduced or paused. After the severance month, you can qualify again if your income falls back below the limit. | | **Both UI **and** severance** | The county adds them together with any other earnings and compares the total to the limit. If the total stays under the limit, you keep receiving CalFresh. | **What to do:** - **Report any UI or severance you start getting** as soon as you receive the first payment. - If the amount is high for a month, the county may **adjust** your CalFresh for that month only; you can still stay enrolled for the following months. --- ## 🏡 Moving to a New County (e.g., living with Mom) 1. **Tell your current county** you’re moving. You can call or send an email with your new address. 2. **Ask for a “transfer”** of your CalFresh case to the new county. Most counties can move the case electronically, which is faster than starting a brand‑new application. 3. **If you can’t transfer** (some counties require a new application), start the application **right away** with the new county so there’s no gap in benefits. 4. **Update your address** in the **EDD UI Online** portal, too—UI payments are sent to the address on file. *Remember:* Every county may have slightly different processing times, so applying early helps keep the food aid coming. --- ## 📋 Other Programs That Might Help You Right Now | Program | Who can apply | What it gives | How to start | |---------|---------------|---------------|--------------| | **CalWORKs** | Low‑income families with children | Cash monthly for housing, utilities, clothing, and more | Call **County Human Services** or apply online at **[CalWORKs portal](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calworks)** | | **Medi‑Cal (California Medicaid)** | Same income rules as CalFresh | Free or low‑cost health coverage for you and your kids | Apply at **[GetMediCal.org](https://www.getmedi-cal.org)** | | **California Training Benefits (CTB)** | You’re receiving UI and want job training | UI continues while you attend approved classes | Ask the **EDD** or visit **[CTB page](https://edd.ca.gov/Training/)** | | **Lifeline Phone/Internet Discount** | If you receive CalFresh, Medicaid, SSI, etc. | Up to $9.25/month discount on phone or internet | Apply at **[LifelineSupport.org](https://www.lifelinesupport.org)** with your benefit proof | | **Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)** | Families with rent arrears due to job loss | One‑time cash help for rent and utilities | Check **[Your county’s ERA site](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/Program/California-Bridge-to-Home)** | --- ## ✅ Quick To‑Do Checklist | ✅ Step | Action | |--------|--------| | 1 | **Apply for CalFresh** now (online or by phone). | | 2 | Gather the **documents** listed above – you can upload them later if you don’t have everything right away. | | 3 | **Report UI or severance** as soon as you receive any payments. | | 4 | If you move, **notify both your current county and the new county** (or start a new application). | | 5 | Look at **other benefits** (CalWORKs, Medi‑Cal, CTB, Lifeline) that can help with housing, health, or training. | | 6 | Keep an eye on your **email or mail** from the county – they may ask for extra info. Reply quickly to avoid delays. | --- ## 🌟 You’re Not Alone Losing a job is stressful, especially with kids. The state has many programs designed to give you food, health care, and help you get back to work. Start the applications today, keep your paperwork organized, and let each agency know about any changes (new job, UI, severance, or moving). If you get stuck, call your **county CalFresh office** – they can walk you through each step. *Wishing you a smooth transition and steady support.*
